events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $10.36 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip (metered, total $38.70 including distance $25.77 for 18.3 km) [F6], so extra kilometres from an unexcused deviation flow straight into the fare and are refundable under RD-2; the trace confirms exactly one off-route segment, 09:12–09:26, driving 9.41 km where the optimal route covers 2.05 km, adding 7.35 km [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

The driver's stated reason — Ayer Rajah Expressway crawling and flooding, "so I went round it" — appears only in his post-trip statement, not in the chat [F8]. The RD-4(a) incident screen fails: no incident was reported on the replaced stretch [F12][RD-4]. A speed-band record does not exempt on its own — Ayer Rajah Expressway at band 2 (10–19 km/h) ending 09:12 is only corroborative [F9], and the other corridor records (Central Expressway, Kent Ridge Road at band 4) are even less supportive [F10][F11], so RD-4(c) sends the segment to RD-2 [RD-4][RD-2]. Heavy rain [F13] does not by itself create the "reasonable cause" RD-4 requires.

No exemption can be found in the chat: there are no in-app messages at all [F7], so no rider message before 09:12:10 agreed to a driver-named road or area, and the driver's claim of agreement exists only in his own statement, which under G11 is not consent — the complete chat record therefore yields "counts", not "undetermined" [F7][F8][RD-5]. Nor is there any rider-named stop: nothing in the record shows a rider naming a place the car stopped at [F7][RD-3]. The segment is therefore non-exempt and the fare difference is refundable [F3][RD-2].

Amount: 7.35 extra km × the trip's per-km rate of $1.4097 (distance fare $25.77 ÷ 18.3 km) = $10.3613, i.e. $10.36 [F3][F6][F4][RD-2]. The rider's requested and cheaper computation (7.6 km × $1.41 = $10.68) is the whole-trip excess rather than the measured unexcused segment, so it is rejected [F4][F1][RD-2]. Since the case is established against the driver by the refund exceeding zero but the profile shows no upheld route dispute in 90 days (driver 1 upheld overall, route 0), RD-6 does not attach an account flag [F15][RD-6], and the rider's profile entry is irrelevant to the outcome [F14].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Good news — your dispute is resolved in your favour.

We found one part of your trip where the driver left the best route without a valid reason: a 7.35 km detour. That detour added to your metered taxi fare, so you're getting it back.

You'll receive a $10.36 Ryde voucher. It's added to your Ryde account automatically — your bank or card isn't involved.

Your requested amount was based on the whole trip's extra distance rather than just that detour, so the smaller measured figure applies.

Nothing else changes on your account.

DRIVER: Your dispute review is complete.

The trip included one unexcused off-route segment — a 7.35 km deviation from the best route. The flooding and traffic you described weren't reported as an incident, weren't raised in the chat, and your post-trip statement alone doesn't establish agreement with the rider. So the extra kilometres count as chargeable and are being refunded to the rider.

Amount: $10.36, issued as a Ryde voucher.

No flag has been placed on your account — this is your first upheld route dispute, so your standing is unchanged. Please keep to the suggested route unless there's a genuine reason, and report any incident in-app as it happens.
